info.title: pruna/p-video-upscale
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "pruna/p-video-upscale", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

post.summary: Queued-only: this route answers 403 not_enabled for pruna/p-video-upscale; use POST /v2/models/pruna/p-video-upscale/requests.

schema.description: Request body for `POST /proxy/pruna/v1/predictions/p-video-upscale`. The model is fixed by the route, so the body carries only Pruna's `input` object.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for `pruna/p-video-2`, `pruna/p-video-2-pro-avatar` and `pruna/p-video-2-pro-reference`: the terminal `GET /proxy/pruna/v1/predictions/status/{id}` document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished prediction (`status: succeeded`) rather than the handle the submit returns.
The generated video is at `generation_url`. A failed prediction carries `error` instead (and `moderation` when Pruna's safety checker blocked it), and a canceled one carries only `status` and `message`.

PrunaPVideoUpscaleInput.description: P-Video-Upscale parameters. The job is billed per second of the returned video, measured from the returned file and rounded up to a whole second. The rate is set by `target` and by whether the output frame rate is above 30 fps. When `fps` is omitted, the output keeps the frame rate of `video`, so that rate decides the tier. A `turbo` job bills at the turbo rate for its `target`, at any frame rate. The safety filter is always on; an `enable_safety_filter` value in the request is ignored.

fps.description: Output frame rate (16-60). A rate above the source rate is interpolated. When omitted, the output keeps the source rate.

target.description: Output resolution preset: 720p, 1080p, 2k or 4k. The preset sets the pixel area; a video that is not 16:9 keeps its aspect ratio. A video already larger than the target is not downscaled.

turbo.description: Faster job with slightly lower quality, billed at the turbo rate (about a third of the standard rate) at any frame rate.

video.description: Input video URI, at most 512 MiB. It must be a publicly readable http(s) URL when `fps` is omitted, because its frame rate is read before the job is sent.

PrunaPredictionModeration.description: Pruna's safety-checker verdict. Present on a failed status when content moderation blocked the prediction.

blocked.description: Whether the safety checker blocked the prediction.

can_disable.description: Whether the block comes from a safety filter the request could disable.

categories.description: Content-policy categories that triggered the block, for example sexual.

phase.description: What was screened: input (the submitted request) or output (the generated video).

error.description: Error message. Present when status is failed.

generation_url.description: URL of the finished video. Present when status is succeeded.

status.description: Prediction status: starting, processing, succeeded, failed or canceled.
